title: Validation of an optimised protocol for quantification of microplastics in heterogenous samples: A case study using green turtle chyme
author: Caron, Thomas, et al.

steps.title: Prevent procedural contamination
steps.instruction: Rinse all work surfaces and equipment with reverse osmosis (RO) water, work inside a fume hood, and avoid any plastic tools or containers.

steps.title: Collect and store turtle chyme
steps.instruction: Obtain foreguts from dead or euthanized green turtles (provided by QPWS); a qualified veterinary pathologist performs necropsy, closes anterior and posterior tract ends with non‑plastic strings, extracts the tracts, places them in aluminium trays with foil, freezes at –20 °C within a few hours, then thaws in a refrigerator at 4 °C for 48 h before analysis. Collect chyme into a glass or metal container using a metal spoon or ladle; rinse the tract over a 100 µm steel‑mesh sieve with RO water, add the retained residue to the chyme, and discard the <100 µm filtrate.

steps.title: Remove macro‑debris and rinse
steps.instruction: Visually inspect the collected chyme, manually remove any visible macro‑debris (e.g., rope, fishing line, bags, bottle lids), rinse each piece over a 100 µm steel‑mesh sieve with RO water, add the retained residue to the chyme, and discard the <100 µm filtrate.

steps.title: Homogenise chyme
steps.instruction: Stir the chyme with a metal spoon for exactly one minute; avoid excessive mechanical stirring or sonication to prevent further fragmentation of brittle plastics. Ensure thorough homogenisation, especially if only a subsample will be analysed.

steps.title: Weigh chyme and plan digestion
steps.instruction: Weigh the homogenised chyme to determine how many 50 mL test tubes are needed and the volume of concentrated nitric acid (HNO₃) required (see next step).

steps.title: Acid digestion of organic material
steps.instruction: For each 50 mL test tube, place approximately 6 g wet weight of homogenised chyme (split into multiple tubes if >6 g) using a metal teaspoon; add 18 mL concentrated HNO₃ (ratio 3 mL acid per 1 g chyme). Cover tubes with aluminium foil and let stand overnight at room temperature (~20 °C). Uncover and heat in a block heater at 80 °C for 2 h, monitoring closely; gently stir with a glass rod as needed to keep material immersed and minimise foaming. While still warm, filter the digest through a 100 µm steel‑mesh sieve folded into a cone and secured with a paper clip into a suitably sized glass beaker; collect retained material in the sieve. Neutralise the acid filtrate by pouring it down the sink followed by ten‑fold its volume of tap water. Rinse the retained material in the sieve with RO water, discard the rinse filtrate. Inspect the material in the sieve for undigested fat residue or sediment to decide the next step: if fat present → emulsification; else if sediment present → density separation; else proceed to filtration.

steps.title: Emulsify residual fats (if present)
steps.instruction: If fat residue is observed, prepare a warm 1 g L⁻¹ sodium lauryl sulphate (SLS) solution by dissolving SLS pellets in RO water on a hot plate set to 50 °C, stirring with a glass rod until clear, and keep at 50 °C. Transfer the residue retained on the 100 µm sieve into the warm SLS solution by placing the sieve upside‑down over a 200 mL glass beaker and rinsing with ~50 mL SLS (or enough to collect all material), then add additional SLS solution to reach a final volume of 200 mL. Sonicate the suspension for 30 s in an ultrasonic bath (47 kHz ± 6%)—no longer sonication. While still warm, filter the suspension over the 100 µm sieve using the same conical‑fold method. Discard the SLS filtrate down the sink with ten‑fold its volume of tap water. Repeat the rinse‑filter cycle until no fat residue remains on the sieve. Finally, rinse the retained material with RO water, discard the rinse, and inspect for sediment; if sediment is present, continue to density separation, otherwise proceed to filtration.

steps.title: Density separation of sediments (if needed)
steps.instruction: If sediment is present, prepare a hypersaline brine of density 1.2 g cm⁻³ by adding NaCl to RO water while stirring continuously until no more dissolves (solubility at 20 °C = 357 g L⁻¹). Transfer the material retained on the 100 µm sieve into 200 mL of this brine by rinsing the sieve over a 200 mL glass beaker with ~50 mL brine, then adding extra brine to reach 200 mL. Stir the suspension for 30 s with a glass rod, rinsing the rod into the beaker. Cover the beaker with aluminium foil and let stand for 1 h to allow separation. Using a glass Pasteur pipette, collect the top ~20 mL of supernatant and transfer to a clean 200 mL glass beaker; rinse the pipette three times with RO water into the same beaker to recover any adhering particles. Discard the remaining ~180 mL of brine together with the settled sediment.

steps.title: Vacuum filtration onto membrane
steps.instruction: Filter the low‑density supernatant obtained from the density‑separation step (or, if density separation was not performed, the material retained on the 100 µm sieve after acid digestion or emulsification) under vacuum onto a 0.45 µm pore‑size membrane filter. Rinse the walls of the 200 mL beaker with RO water into the vacuum‑filter apparatus at least three times (or until all particles are recovered). After filtration, rinse the funnel walls three times with RO water using a pipette. Using metal tweezers, place each filter into a covered glass dish.

steps.title: Dry and inspect filters
steps.instruction: Oven‑dry the filters at 60 °C for 4 h. After cooling, visually inspect each filter under a dissecting microscope for microplastic particles.

steps.title: FTIR analysis of microplastics
steps.instruction: No further treatment of the particles is required. For macro‑plastics recovered earlier, rinse thoroughly with RO water and oven‑dry at 60 °C for 4 h before analysis. Place individual particles on the ATR diamond of a PerkinElmer Spectrum 100 FTIR spectrometer (ATR accessory) using tweezers or needles, and secure with a pressure clamp. Acquire spectra in transmission mode with 64 scans, 4 cm⁻¹ resolution, over the 4000–400 cm⁻¹ range. Use the Data Tune‑up command for smoothing and baseline correction with default parameters. Compare spectra against the NICODOM IR library using Euclidian distance; record percent match. Interpret matches as: <60 % low, 60–<70 % intermediate, ≥70 % high. Manually inspect all spectra and investigate any unexplained bands by reviewing lower‑match spectra and the literature to confirm polymer identity.

steps.title: Validate extraction with spiked samples
steps.instruction: Prepare three validation samples by spiking 6 g (wet weight) of homogenised chyme with five HDPE micro‑beads (diameter 192 ± 48 µm). Process these spiked samples through the full sequential protocol (acid digestion, emulsification, density separation). Record recovery; in this study all beads were recovered, giving 100 % extraction efficiency for >100 µm HDPE beads.

steps.title: Run procedural blanks for contamination check
steps.instruction: Prepare three procedural blanks by adding 6 mL RO water to a 50 mL test tube and processing them through the entire sequential protocol. After oven‑drying the resulting filters, inspect them under a dissecting microscope; any particles or fibres observed are recorded as procedural contamination. Note that hair‑like fibres and fine dark particles (~100 µm) were detected in this study; for analyses targeting <100 µm particles, implement stricter contamination controls (e.g., synthetic‑free clothing, sealed damp‑wiped workspace).
